reviewed_sections: Limits, source rights and future falsifiers

author_reported_results: WT first daughter refractory 46.5±4.5% versus second 12.2±3.3%; shs1 deletion first 66.9±6.3%, second 30.4±12.3%. First division frequently abnormal septin and barrier weaker with post-pheromone mean indices 10.80 vs 12.86 untreated.

paper_version: Primary full main text 2014
review_scope: complete primary PLOS article and main methods/figures; supplements and data unexecuted.
method_notes: Chemoflux external nutrient switching, measured growth in five chambers, LacZ/LacY/LacA perturbations and LacY fluorescence; mathematical flux model separated from assays.
author_reported_results: First glucose-to-lactose shift produces roughly 35-minute growth lag and 55-minute full recovery in chemoflux E coli. Lac protein carryover makes later exposure to lactose less costly, with memory fading through dilution over cell divisions. Response memory can boost lactose use by up to 100 percent under fast fluctuations according to the authors' mathematical model.
limitations: Externally controlled feed and pre-existing lac circuitry; five chambers are not independent evolution replicates; modeled doubled flux does not equal measured doubled cell fitness. Native metabolic machinery and researcher-supplied alternating media prevent claims of newly evolved learning. Persistent physiology is not an organism inventing its own forgetting controller or mental representation. This is a modeled lactose flux difference, not a measured two-fold cell survival or lifetime fitness improvement.

paper_version: Primary full main text 2024
review_scope: whole original open author manuscript and main methods/figures; raw sequencing/source code not run.
method_notes: Original selection from 500k barcoded yeast lines, 1-2 evolutionary flasks per environment, 889 selected clones, three later fitness assay replicates, 695 core adaptive filter and 352 genomes.
author_reported_results: The authors find 53 percent of environmental component-history fitness measurements exceed their conservative significance threshold. The other static environment better predicts a current fluctuating-component fitness measurement in 29 percent of studied cases. Only one or two original evolution flasks per condition contributed to the 889 selected barcoded mutants analyzed using three fitness assay replicates.
limitations: Clones and assay replicates are not independent evolution cohorts; barcoded competition measures context fitness rather than within-cell learning; lag-shift model not causally reconstructed. Percentage is of their defined pooled fitness assay observations, not independently created living organisms. This is a statistical performance reversal under previous exposure, not conscious forecasting or an active learned goal. Do not treat the hundreds of barcodes or pooled fitness measurements as hundreds of independent evolutionary origins.

paper_version: Primary full main text 2008
review_scope: complete PLOS ONE main methods, figures and discussion; original MATLAB/assay files not reanalyzed.
method_notes: Ten past histories from two media x five culture densities, three cultures each, standardized starvation, population GFP sporulation, DsRed AprE and optical density over transient and later windows.
author_reported_results: Bacillus sporulation-reporter response carries roughly 1.96 bits of short-time history and 0.8813 bits at the final finite measurement window. The authors explicitly consider metabolic initial state as an alternative to an evolved future-predictive strategy.
limitations: Information extraction depends on defined history classes, clustering and population-averaged reporters; molecular cause, inherited ability and later fitness were not demonstrated. The maximum 3.3219 bits reflects ten investigator-selected past conditions, not a physical limit on memory or a life score. High mutual information about past conditions does not establish causal ecological benefit, intentional prediction or subjective experience.

paper_version: Primary full main text 2000
review_scope: full original public 5-page primary PNAS article, control assumptions and comparison to prior evidence.
method_notes: Five-page mathematical control systems interpretation of bacterial CheR/CheB receptor methylation, CheA, CheY-P and CheZ feedback, comparing to existing published experimental evidence.
author_reported_results: Receptor methylation and demethylation can implement integral feedback that restores adapted bacterial chemotaxis output after stimulation. Robust return of a chemotactic output to baseline is compatible with a hidden physical history state maintained within signaling machinery.
limitations: Fixed previously evolved chemotaxis machinery is assumed; analytic adaptation under a defined regime is not de novo cognition or an independently reproduced organism. Existing sensor network and model assumptions are specified; it does not show the organism invented adaptive learning circuitry. A smooth feedback response can look intelligent without novel learning, subjective experience or evolutionary self-creation.
